children: chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan plans to leave the company in 2027, ending a tenure of more than 15 years as a key adviser to CEO Mark Zuckerberg on political and regulatory matters, Axios reported.
Kaplan joined Facebook when the company was developing its approach to government relations and went on to establish its U.S. policy team. Before joining Meta
, he served as deputy White House chief of staff under former President George W. Bush and worked as a Marine artillery officer.
He played a significant role in shaping Meta's

response to regulatory scrutiny, including efforts to protect its personalized advertising model, according to the report. Kaplan also supported Zuckerberg's approach to free expression and helped foster ties with the incoming Trump administration.
Zuckerberg praised Kaplan's contributions, telling Axios that he had been involved in nearly every major challenge confronting the company over more than 15 years.

Kaplan is expected to remain in his position through the U.S. midterm elections and into 2027 to facilitate a leadership transition involving executives with experience across both major political parties.
As part of the changes, Meta

President and Vice Chairman Dina Powell McCormick will assume additional external affairs responsibilities. Chief Legal Officer C.J. Mahoney will also take on policy duties, while Brian Rice and Tucker Bounds will contribute through their respective government affairs and communications roles.

title: Meta's global affairs chief Joel Kaplan to step down next year
